entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is the second application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S. for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.09/2025 registered at Police Station Ganj, District Betul (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC.
The applicant is in custody since 07.05.2025.

The first application of applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 31.07.2025 passed in MCRC. No.28978/2025.
2.

As per the prosecution story, the allegation against present applicant is that he alongwith co-accused persons committed fraud upon complainant of Rs.11,50,000/- on the pretext of providing job in foreign and given forged appointment letter to the complainant.
Therefore, offence has been registered against the present applicant and co-accused persons under the aforesaid sections.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He is in custody since 07.05.2025.
It is submitted that only allegation against present applicant is that he has forwarded appointment letter to the complainant on WhatsApp.
He has not made NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50700 2 MCRC-39729-2025 any forged document.
It is further submitted that date of incident is 02.11.2021 whereas FIR was lodged on 07.01.2025.
Charge sheet has been filed.
The conclusion of the trial will take considerable time, therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer of bail and has submitted that in this case present applicant has made forged documents visa etc. and received money from the complainant through R.T.G.S. and cheques.

He has issued forged appointment letter to the Rohit Thul vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147391599/
1 complainant.

sentences.text: Two mobiles have also been seized from the present applicant.
Hence, the applicant does not deserve grant of bail.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.
Looking to aforesaid facts and circumstances as well as seriousness of the offence, I am not inclined to grant bail to the present applicant.
7. Accordingly, present MCRC stands dismissed.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE mohsin Rohit Thul vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147391599/
